### policy_conflict_scan
- **Base copy verbatim**: every top-level key of the base charter (`category, display_name, binding, lifecycle, accounts, parameter_schema, variants, events, measures, policies`) is byte-identical between `products/financing.yaml` and the `financing.extended.yaml` base section (checked by structural equality after YAML load).
- **Seven extended policies**, each claiming one `(target_tool, computes)`:
  | policy | trigger | subject | tool (owner) | computes |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | financing_ext_settlement_figure | on_request | financing_plan_closed_paid, financing_payment_posted | confirm_plan_settlement_d71750ce (user) | settlement_amount |
  | financing_ext_returned_payment_charge | state_due | financing_returned_payment_fee_assessed | book_returned_payment_charge_6a9e81de (agent) | charge_amount |
  | financing_ext_lateness_charge | state_due | financing_late_fee_assessed | book_lateness_charge_0092ea40 (agent) | lateness_charge |
  | financing_ext_cycle_statement | state_due | financing_statement_issued | issue_cycle_statement_c71da302 (agent) | statement_amount |
  | financing_ext_service_recovery_giveback | state_due | financing_fee_waiver_applied | apply_service_recovery_giveback_b70a9c9e (agent) | giveback_amount |
  | financing_ext_schedule_rebuild | state_due | financing_plan_terms_updated | update_scheduled_payment_2c04479a (agent) | rebuilt_monthly_payment |
  | financing_ext_hardship_schedule | on_request | financing_hardship_enrolled | confirm_hardship_schedule_eb08e7db (user) | reduced_payment_amount |
- **Overlapping subjects**: no two extended policies share a subject event or a tool. `financing_payment_posted` (settlement) and `financing_hardship_enrolled` (hardship) are also base subjects of `financing_evt_payment_allocation` / `financing_hardship_arrangement`; those base policies are named in `base_policy_refs` and their eligibility sentences are inherited (see override_declarations).
- **Time anchors**: every extended rule anchors on "the handling date" (= `frozen_time` date) and on record dates (`activated_date`, statement `posted_date`, `payment_due_date`, `last_payment_date`). Whole-month counting is `MONTHS(d1,d2)` (calendar months, decremented when the handling day-of-month is earlier than the anchor's), windows are `0 <= MONTHS(row_date, NOW) < N`. Base grace/validity/cooling-off counting sentences are inherited untouched. No two policies count the same window differently for the same quantity: each policy defines its own "stretch" and names it in its own rule.
- **Terminal states**: settlement tool → `status=paid_off, current_balance=0, closed_date, last_payment_date` + a settled `financing_payment_posted` row (base transition past_due/active/in_hardship → paid_off); hardship tool → `status=in_hardship, hardship_plan_code, scheduled_monthly_payment` (base transition active/past_due → in_hardship); the five agent tools each add one ledger row or update `scheduled_monthly_payment` only. No policy's terminal state contradicts another's.
- **Cross-category read boundaries**: settlement reads tradein (`status, remaining_credit, issued_credit_amount, credit_partially_redeemable`); returned-payment reads protection (`status, premium_payment_schedule, protection_ledger.event_type`); lateness reads service (`status, rework_count`); cycle_statement reads protection (`status, claims_settled_count, premium_amount, premium_payment_schedule`); giveback reads service (`status, promised_date, rework_count`); rebuild reads protection (`status, remaining_benefit_allowance, deductible_amount, premium_amount, premium_payment_schedule`); hardship reads custom (`status, balance_due`). Every field read is a real column of that holding table in `db_schema.json` or a real variant parameter of that product's charter (`premium_payment_schedule` on all six protection variants; `credit_partially_redeemable` on all six tradein variants). Every branch value named is a real lifecycle state of that product (`active`; `in_workshop`, `awaiting_authorization`; `in_production`, `design_approval`; `credit_issued`, `partially_redeemed`). All are reachable through `share_tools.py` finders (`find_tradein_credits`, `find_protection_plans`, `find_protection_ledger`, `find_service_orders`, `find_custom_orders`).
- **Task scopes**: the `prerequisite` graph partitions the seven policies into two trees — tree A = {settlement_figure ← returned_payment_charge, lateness_charge} and tree B = {hardship_schedule ← schedule_rebuild ← cycle_statement, service_recovery_giveback}. Two trees, M=2: mutually exclusive and jointly complete over the extended policies. (Which task holds which tree is a per-task fact and is recorded in the task files.)

### rule_compute_equivalence
Every `compute` binding of every policy carries a `compute_basis` quotation that is a verbatim sentence of that policy's `rule` (checked by substring for all 7 policies). Sweep, policy by policy:
- **settlement_figure**: plan_balance ← "balance the plan record carries at the handling date"; review_window_months (3-tier), settled_payments_in_review/missed_cycles ← "missed cycles are the length of the stretch less the settled payments credited in it, never fewer than none"; settlement_apr (3-tier); last_statement_date/latest_due_date/settled_recently/interest_days (3-tier anchor); period_interest ← "balance × rate / 100 × days / year-days, rounded to the cent at that point" (`K('day_count_year_days')=365`); charge_window_months (3-tier); late_charges/returned_charges/givebacks/standing_charges ← charges "taken together with the give-backs ... which are negative"; credit_* / credit_offset (3-tier); result ← "added, rounded to the cent, floored at nothing" and "credit ... taken off the sum before it is rounded". Both directions close. The rule additionally carries the baseline sentences ("The settlement rate is the term's promotional rate." / "counted from the closing date of the most recent statement" / "the term's repeat window") beside the ladders that generalise them — the baseline+ladder topology of this charter; the ladder's fall-through equals the baseline sentence in every case, so the merged reading is unique.
- **returned_payment_charge**: months_billing, returns_window_months (3-tier), returns_count/base_fee (3-tier, `repeat_return_pct=25`, `clean_history_relief_pct=40`), returned_channel/returns_this_cycle/channel_relief (3-tier; "channel the term credits on the day it is received" implemented as the literal set `in_store|online_portal|phone_agent` — matches `same_day_credit_channels` of every variant except that the 48-Month term also lists `autopay`, which compute omits: an autopay-channel return on a 48-Month plan would get the same-day allowance under the rule and none under compute — recorded as observation O-3), coverage_* (3-tier, XCOUNT over `protection_ledger` within 3 months), down_payment_share/tenure_relief_amount (3-tier), result. Closed.
- **lateness_charge**: repeat_window_months (3-tier), prior_late_fees/prior_givebacks/standing_late_fees (3-tier), base_charge (3-tier, `early_tenure_charge_pct=50`, `early_tenure_months=6`), missed_due_date ← `LATEST(payment_due_date of returned payments)` — the rule's "the missed due date" is implemented as the due date carried by the most recently posted returned payment; the prose never says which due date is "the missed due date" when several are unanswered (observation O-4, per-task consequence checked in the task files); assessed_days_past_due (3-tier); months_since_due/delinquency_uplift (3-tier, 30% / 10%); service_* / relationship_relief (3-tier) — prose "a piece with the workshop that the chain has not yet handed back" is implemented as `status in {in_workshop, awaiting_authorization}`, narrower than the prose (a piece at `intake`, `estimated` or `ready_for_pickup` is also not yet handed back) — observation O-5; result. Otherwise closed.
- **cycle_statement**: settled_in_cycle/returned_in_cycle/payment_due_component (3-tier), charge_window_months (3-tier, `statement_lookback_months=2`), late_in_window/presentation_share (3-tier, 0 / 50 / 100)/charge_component, coverage_* (3-tier), result. Closed.
- **service_recovery_giveback**: charge_window_months (3-tier, ×2), late_charges_in_window/givebacks_in_window/givebacks_count/latest_charge_amount/charge_base (3-tier), returns_in_review/failure_addition (3-tier, 30 / 15), service_* / workshop_addition (3-tier, 40 / 20) — prose "a piece with the workshop that the chain promised for a date already past and has not yet handed back" implemented as `status == 'in_workshop' and DAYS(promised_date, NOW) > 0` (narrower on status, same as O-5); result ← "booked against the most recently booked lateness charge and carries the whole of that sum". Closed.
- **schedule_rebuild**: adjust_window_months (3-tier), givebacks_recent/balance_now, returns_in_window/applicable_rate (3-tier), payment_factor_pct (3-tier, 4.5 / 2.4 / term factor), principal_component, last_statement_date/interest_component (3-tier: actual/365, actual/360, nominal/365), returns_this_month/returned_amount_month/catchup_component (3-tier, spread over `hardship_term_months`), coverage_* / coverage_component (3-tier, `coverage_servicing_amount=3.5`), result. Closed.
- **hardship_schedule**: arrangement_months (3-tier), returned_amount_month/ordinary_payment (3-tier), hardship_share_pct (3-tier, 75 / 45 / term share), reduced_base, balance_for_interest/returns_in_review/rate_component (3-tier), returns_this_month/arrangement_setup_charge (3-tier, 5 / 2.5 / 7.5), commission_*/commitment_relief (3-tier, 15 / 8), result ← "hardship share applied ... rounded; interest and charge added, relief taken off; rounded at the end only; floored at nothing". - Every ladder tier named in `factors[].ladder` is a clause of the rule and a branch of the `decides` binding, and every branch of every `decides` binding is a tier the rule states (checked for all 33 factors). No tier lives only in compute.

### prerequisite_graph
- `prerequisite` is filled on all seven policies (`[]` on returned_payment_charge, lateness_charge, cycle_statement, service_recovery_giveback).
- Edges (blocked → depended-on | kind | gate | form):
  1. settlement_figure → returned_payment_charge | value_input | standing_charges | state
  2. settlement_figure → lateness_charge | value_input | standing_charges | state
  3. schedule_rebuild → cycle_statement | value_input | interest_component | state
  4. schedule_rebuild → service_recovery_giveback | value_input | balance_now | state
  5. hardship_schedule → schedule_rebuild | value_input | ordinary_payment | state
- Every `problem` is an extended policy id of this file (never base, never self); the graph is acyclic (two trees, depth 1 and depth 2). Every `policy_source` is a verbatim substring of the blocked policy's own `rule` (checked). `form` is `state` on all five; no `fallback_reason` is present and none is required. `resolved_by` equals the depended-on policy's `target_tool` on all five. Every `gate` is a binding name that exists in the blocked policy's `compute` (`standing_charges`, `interest_component`, `balance_now`, `ordinary_payment`), so `kind: value_input` matches `gate` on all five. No authoring-viewpoint phrasing ("in this task", "at the opening") appears in any `prerequisite` field.
- `condition` versus sentence: edges 1, 3, 5 carry the sentence's strength exactly. Edge 2's `condition` ("Every payment due date printed on a statement of the plan that no settled payment answers carries a lateness charge") is broader than its sentence ("every **missed** payment due date"): an unanswered due date still inside the term's grace is unanswered but, under the inherited base sentence "equality with that boundary does not yet make the payment late", not missed — observation O-8; the base grace sentence closes the gap to one reading, and the task files check whether such a due date exists in each world. Edge 4's `condition` and sentence agree ("every lateness charge ... that a failure of the chain's own handling brought about") but neither names a record field that marks a charge as chain-caused; how a reader identifies that charge is a per-world question recorded in the task files (O-9).
- `effect` claims are consistent with the bindings: edges 1–2 add rows the `standing_charges` sums pick up; edge 3 moves `last_statement_date`, which `interest_component` reads only on its past-due and autopay tiers (on the fall-through tier the interest runs on the nominal cycle length and the edge cannot bear weight through this binding — per-task check); edge 4 adds a negative give-back row that `givebacks_recent` sums into `balance_now`; edge 5 changes `F('scheduled_monthly_payment')`, which `ordinary_payment` reads.

### prerequisite_sentences
Four-point test on each edge's sentence (all state form):
1. "The settlement figure is worked out only after every payment the bank has sent back unpaid on the plan carries the returned-payment charge owed against it in the billing history." — own result ("settlement figure is worked out") + connective ("only after") + record-visible state (a returned payment entry carrying a returned-payment charge in the billing history — the ledger's `payment_outcome = returned_*` rows and `financing_returned_payment_fee_assessed` rows with `source_entry_id`) + no tool/id/snake_case. Strength: "every" — universal over the plan's returned payments, matching the condition. One write brings the state about: `book_returned_payment_charge_6a9e81de` is the only tool creating `financing_returned_payment_fee_assessed`. Derivation: sentence → records show a returned payment with no charge against it → the returned-payment-charge policy's rule ("charged against the returned payment entry itself") → its tool. Single reading.
2. "The settlement figure is worked out only after every missed payment due date printed on the plan's statements carries the lateness charge due against it in the billing history." — same four points; state = a statement's `payment_due_date` with a `financing_late_fee_assessed` row for that due date. One write: `book_lateness_charge_0092ea40`. Derivation: sentence → statements' due dates with no settled payment and past grace → lateness policy → its tool. Single reading once the base grace sentence is applied (O-8).
3. "The rebuilt payment is fixed only after every billing cycle the plan has closed carries in the billing history the statement that cycle presented." — state = a `financing_statement_issued` row per closed cycle. One write: `issue_cycle_statement_c71da302`. Derivation: statement day on the plan record → cycles closed up to the handling date → missing statement rows → cycle-statement policy → its tool. Single reading.
4. "Before the rebuilt payment is worked out, every lateness charge the plan carries that a failure of the chain's own handling brought about must already stand answered by a give-back in the billing history." — connective "before"; state = a `financing_fee_waiver_applied` row whose `source_entry_id` is that charge. One write: `apply_service_recovery_giveback_b70a9c9e` (the only tool creating `financing_fee_waiver_applied`). Which charge "a failure of the chain's own handling brought about" is not a ledger field; the sentence is resolvable only where the world or the customer makes the chain's failure evident (O-9, per task).
5. "The reduced payment is worked out only once the scheduled monthly payment the plan record carries answers the balance the plan owes at the handling date." — connective "only once"; state = the plan record's `scheduled_monthly_payment` equalling what the balance produces. One write: `update_scheduled_payment_2c04479a` (the hardship tool also writes `scheduled_monthly_payment`, but to the reduced figure — it is the blocked policy's own write, not a candidate for the waited-on state). Derivation: sentence → compare the record's payment with the rebuilt figure → schedule-rebuild policy → its tool. Single reading.
- No rule carries a second wording of any dependency, a tool name or another policy's id; no depended-on rule restates the sentence; no base sentence grounds any edge; no rule states a cross-problem order that grounds no edge. State form is honoured throughout, so no `fallback_reason` is tested.

### override_declarations
Sentence by sentence against each `base_policy_refs` entry:
- **settlement_figure ↔ financing_closure_and_payoff**: "A plan begins billing only while it stands approved..." (inherited, untouched); "A payoff figure is the current balance together with any held-back interest..." (**declared**); "honoured at settlement only when the handling date has not passed the validity window of the quote" + counting sentence (inherited; the figure is quoted and settled on the handling date, so the window is trivially met); "closes settled on the day the last payment or credit posted, residual at or below the write-off threshold written off" (inherited; the tool closes on the handling date with balance 0 — consistent); "A payoff quote is taken on the financing service request record and the settlement itself is made by the customer" (inherited; tool owner=user). ↔ **financing_evt_payment_allocation**: allocation order (inherited; tool books `allocation_bucket=mixed`, no quantity depends on it); "posted only while ... approved, active, past due or in a hardship arrangement" (inherited state gate); same-day channel/cut-off (inherited; the tool posts on `phone_agent`, a same-day channel on the 24/36/48-Month terms and not on the 6/12/18-Month terms — per-task check of term and clock); "clearing the plan early carries the term's prepayment charge" (inherited; `prepayment_penalty_pct = 0.0` on every term, so no entry arises); returned payment reversal (inherited). Every sentence concluded; one conflict, declared.
- **returned_payment_charge ↔ financing_evt_returned_payment**: fee sentence (**declared**); dedup "only when no returned payment fee already stands against that same returned payment entry" (inherited); per-cycle ceiling (inherited; the extended rule does not restate it and compute does not implement it — a return beyond the ceiling would be charged by compute and not by base: observation O-10, consequence only on a world with ≥cap fees already in the cycle); bank-error give-back (inherited). One conflict, declared.
- **lateness_charge ↔ financing_evt_late_fee**: "carries a late fee once the term's grace period has run out" and "charged only when the handling date has passed the due date extended by the grace period; equality does not yet make it late" + counting sentence (inherited eligibility, per task); "only while the plan stands at active or past due" (inherited); first/repeat sentence (**declared**); "No single late fee exceeds the term's ceiling expressed as a share of the scheduled monthly payment" (inherited; extended compute carries no cap — observation O-11, consequence only where the computed charge exceeds `late_fee_cap_pct × scheduled payment`); "one fee per missed due date and never more than one" (inherited, consistent with the tool's one-row-per-call); autopay-failure non-charge (inherited). One conflict, declared.
- **cycle_statement ↔ financing_evt_statement_cycle**: statement day / due date lead sentence (inherited; the tool takes `closing_date` and `payment_due_date` as arguments, so the base fixes them); "produced only while active, past due or in hardship, and only when the balance reaches the threshold" (inherited); scheduled-payment sentence (**declared**); delivery channel and paper fee (inherited; `paper_statement_fee` is 1.99 on the 6/12/18-Month terms and 0.0 on the 24/36/48-Month terms — on a paper-delivered deferred-interest plan a servicing-fee entry would be due under base and no extended policy books it: observation O-12, per-task); skip/write-off sentence and servicing-entry sentence (inherited). One conflict, declared.
- **service_recovery_giveback ↔ financing_courtesy_waiver**: allowance count (inherited, not consumed); "granted against a late fee only when no give-back already stands against that same late fee entry" and "never granted against a charge that has already been given back" (inherited — the extended rule books "against the most recently booked lateness charge"; if that charge already carries a give-back the base forbids the write: per-task check); tenure sentences (courtesy only, inherited); bank-error/service-failure sentence (**declared**); exhausted-allowance sentence (courtesy only). One conflict, declared.
- **schedule_rebuild ↔ financing_return_credit**: rebuild sentence (**declared**); every other sentence of return_credit governs the return credit itself, not touched. ↔ **financing_hardship_arrangement**: "enrolled, and the servicing details it changes are written, only while the plan stands at active, past due or in an existing hardship arrangement" (inherited state gate on `financing_plan_terms_updated`); all other sentences untouched. Observation O-13: the quantity the rebuild writes (`scheduled_monthly_payment`) is the one base `financing_evt_statement_cycle` fixes as "the larger of the floor and the factor applied to the balance at the start of the term"; schedule_rebuild does not name that base sentence in its own `overwrite`, but the same sentence is declared superseded by `financing_ext_cycle_statement` in this same charter, so no live base clause competes with the rebuilt figure. The base payment floor (`minimum_monthly_payment_floor`) is not restated by the rebuild and not implemented in its compute (per-task check whether the rebuilt figure falls below the floor).
- **hardship_schedule ↔ financing_hardship_arrangement**: replacement sentence (inherited); state gate (inherited); reduced-payment sentence (**declared**); "never enrolled in more arrangements than the term allows ... not yet billing for the minimum hardship tenure is not enrolled at all" (inherited eligibility, per task); "taken on the financing service request record and only takes effect once the customer confirms" (inherited; tool owner=user); breakdown sentence (inherited). One conflict, declared.
- No anonymous intermediate, 0/1 multiplier or dropped branch found: every base branch that survives is either inherited unchanged or named in `overwrite`. No author note calls a base output "wrong".

- Counts: every policy declares 4–6 factors, ≥2 `parameter`, ≥1 `method`; every policy has a `cross_difficulty` factor and at least one multi-source factor, so any task built on any of these policies meets the per-task floors structurally.
- Bindings: each factor's `bindings` set is disjoint from every other factor's in the same policy; `decides` is never `result`.
- Label honesty: every `parameter` factor's tiers substitute a number (a rate, a fee, a share, an allowance, a credit amount); every `method` factor's tiers change an anchor date, a window length, a day-count convention or which rows are read. Every method tier names a rule the charter states in its own prose.
- Distinct outcomes: no two tiers of any ladder select the same value or method as stated. (On a given world two tiers can coincide numerically — e.g. `remaining_credit == issued_credit_amount` on a fresh registration — but the tiers differ as stated.)
- Business realism: every condition is one a consumer-credit desk weighs for that quantity (delinquency standing, return history, autopay, tenure, down-payment share, channel, coverage held, workshop standing, commission standing, hardship in force); every fall-through is the term's own published figure or nothing; no condition holds of every customer who reaches the write (each tier's condition is falsified by some plan the policy admits).
- Tiers stated in the rule and implemented in compute: all 33 ladders, checked both ways.
- **Overlap as stated (finding F-1)**: in five ladders the first two tiers are not pairwise disjoint as worded, the compute resolving the overlap by first-match order: settlement none; `lateness_history_window` (tier 1 "past due ∧ return this month" ∩ tier 2 "billing fewer months than the repeat window"); `lateness_clock_anchor` (tier 1 "autopay ∧ return this month" ∩ tier 2 "past due ∧ no settled payment this month"); `presented_charge_window` (tier 1 "return this month" ∩ tier 2 "billing fewer months than the repeat window"); `coverage_presentation_band` (tier 1 "in force ∧ monthly premium" ∩ tier 2 "in force ∧ no claim settled"); `carried_coverage_amount` (tier 1 "in force ∧ monthly premium" ∩ tier 2 "in force ∧ allowance above deductible"). The remaining 28 ladders are disjoint as stated (the author disjointified them explicitly, e.g. "no payment has been sent back unpaid and a settled payment stands"). Whether a task's customer sits in an overlap region — where the prose alone yields two values — is demonstrated, if at all, in that task's file.

### findings
- **F-1 (observation unless a task's world sits in the overlap; charter-global)** — five ladders with tiers that overlap as stated (list above). Root cause: tier 2's condition does not exclude tier 1's. Evidence: quoted conditions in `factor_ladders`. Consequence: on a world in the overlap, the rule prose gives two values and only compute's order picks one; bears on any task whose customer is in the overlap (checked per task).
- **O-2 (observation)** — `financing_ext_returned_payment_charge.baseline.rule` names three allowances ("the channel allowance, the coverage allowance and the standing allowance") but assigns no default to any of them, whereas every other baseline states its defaults outright ("The delinquency uplift is nothing. The relationship allowance is nothing." etc.). A reader of the baseline alone has to conclude that an allowance with no stated amount is nothing; the number is still definite (the base fee). `baseline.params` (`returned_payment_fee, returned_payment_fee_cap_per_cycle`) names no allowance key. Bears on the task holding tree A.
- **O-3 (observation)** — same-day-channel set hard-coded as `in_store|online_portal|phone_agent`; the 48-Month term also credits `autopay` same-day. No consequence on a non-48-Month plan.
- **O-4 (observation, per-task consequence)** — "the missed due date" in the lateness rule is implemented as the due date carried by the most recently posted returned payment; where the world has more than one unanswered due date past grace, the prose does not say which is priced first.
- **O-5 (observation)** — "not yet handed back" implemented as `in_workshop|awaiting_authorization` (lateness) and `in_workshop` (giveback); narrower than prose for `intake/estimated/ready_for_pickup`. No consequence where the order stands `in_workshop`.
- **O-6, O-7 (observations)** — docstring wording ("before the call"; enum description mirroring the rule). No consequence.
- **O-8 (observation, per-task)** — edge 2 `condition` ("no settled payment answers") broader than its sentence ("missed"); base grace sentence closes it.
- **O-9 (observation, per-task)** — edge 4's "a failure of the chain's own handling" is not a ledger field; discoverability depends on the world/persona.
- **O-10, O-11, O-12 (observations, per-task)** — inherited base ceilings/fees not restated in extended compute: returned-fee per-cycle cap, late-fee cap as share of scheduled payment, paper statement fee on paper-delivered terms.
- **O-13 (observation)** — schedule_rebuild's `overwrite` does not name base `financing_evt_statement_cycle`'s scheduled-payment sentence; that sentence is superseded by `financing_ext_cycle_statement` in the same charter, so no live base clause competes. The base payment floor is not implemented by the rebuild compute (per-task check).
- **F-2 (charter-global fact, per-task consequence)** — edge 1's sentence and condition are universal ("every payment the bank has sent back unpaid on the plan"); the returned-payment-charge compute prices one return (its channel read as `LATEST`, its cycle count as the current month) and the tool books one row per call. On a world with more than one returned payment lacking a charge the sentence demands as many charges as there are such returns, each priced by the same compute; whether such a world exists is demonstrated in the task files.
